policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ἐὰν and ἂν are interchangeable in the indefinite relative 'whatsoever they bid you'; the ASV wording is identical either way.

ASV 'these do and observe' has two verbs in the order do-then-observe, matching ποιήσατε καὶ τηρεῖτε; the RP reading τηρεῖν τηρεῖτε καὶ ποιεῖτε reverses the order and adds an infinitive that would surface as 'observe to do'.
ASV opens v. 4 with the continuative 'Yea, they bind', not a causal 'For'; δέ is rendered, γάρ is not.

ASV text reads 'heavy burdens and grievous to be borne', and its textual_variant note ('Many ancient authorities omit and grievous to be borne') shows the omission was relegated to the margin; καὶ δυσβάστακτα stands in the text.
ASV 'but they themselves will not move them' renders the emphatic pronoun αὐτοὶ, absent from the RP reading τῷ δέ.
ASV 'for they make broad their phylacteries' renders the causal γάρ; δέ would give 'and/but they make broad'.
ASV 'the borders of their garments' renders τῶν ἱματίων αὐτῶν, which the base lemma lacks.
ASV 'and love the chief place at feasts' renders a bare connective that suits either δέ or τε; the English does not distinguish the particles.
ASV ends v. 7 with a single 'Rabbi.'; the RP doubling Ῥαββί Ῥαββί would surface as 'Rabbi, Rabbi'.
ASV 'for one is your teacher' renders διδάσκαλος alone, with no 'the Christ'; the RP reading καθηγητής ὁ χριστός would add both a different noun and 'the Christ' (as ASV supplies it in v. 10).
Word order only: 'one is your Father' is the same English for ὑμῶν ὁ πατήρ and ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν.
The ASV note 'Greek the heavenly' glosses the underlying word as the adjective οὐράνιος; the RP prepositional phrase ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς would be glossed 'in the heavens', not 'the heavenly'.
ASV 'for one is your master' renders either ὅτι or γάρ as 'for', and the remaining differences are word order and the article; nothing in the English distinguishes them.

ASV prints no widows'-houses woe after v. 12; its textual_variant note at v. 13 ('Some authorities insert here, or after verse 12, verse 14 Woe unto you...') places that material in the margin, so the ASV text ends v. 12 at ὑψωθήσεται and keeps SBL's verse numbering.
ASV opens v. 13 'But woe unto you', rendering δέ, which the RP reading omits.
ASV has no verse 14 in its text; the textual_variant note attributes the widows'-houses woe to 'some authorities', so the added verse is not part of the ASV's Greek.
ASV 'the temple that hath sanctified the gold' renders the aorist participle ἁγιάσας; the ASV marks the tense distinction, rendering the present ἁγιάζον in v. 19 as 'sanctifieth'.
ἂν and ἐὰν are interchangeable after ὃς in 'Whosoever shall swear'; the ASV wording is identical either way.
ASV opens v. 19 'Ye blind:' with no 'Ye fools and'; the RP reading Μωροὶ καὶ τυφλοί would repeat the address of v. 17.
ASV 'him that dwelleth therein' renders the present participle κατοικοῦντι; the aorist κατοικήσαντι would not give a present habitual.
The readings differ only in declension of the same noun (neuter τὸ ἔλεος vs masculine τὸν ἔλεον); ASV 'mercy' does not distinguish them.
ASV 'but these ye ought to have done' renders an adversative δέ after ταῦτα, which the base lemma's asyndeton lacks.
ἀφιέναι and ἀφεῖναι are alternative infinitive forms of the same verb; ASV 'to have left ... undone' does not distinguish them.
The presence or absence of the article οἱ before the participle leaves 'that strain out the gnat' unchanged in English.
ASV 'from extortion and excess' renders ἀκρασίας ('excess', lack of self-control); the RP ἀδικίας would give 'unrighteousness'.
ASV 'the inside of the cup and of the platter' renders καὶ τῆς παροψίδος, which the omission would delete.
ASV 'the outside thereof' is singular, agreeing with αὐτοῦ; the plural αὐτῶν would give 'the outside of them'.
παρομοιάζετε and ὁμοιάζετε are synonymous verbs of resemblance; ASV 'ye are like unto' renders either.
Word order only: ἐστε μεστοὶ and μεστοί ἐστε both give 'ye are full'.
ἤμεθα and ἦμεν are alternative first-person plural imperfect forms of εἰμί; ASV 'If we had been' does not distinguish them.
ἤμεθα and ἦμεν are alternative first-person plural imperfect forms of εἰμί; ASV 'we should not have been partakers' does not distinguish them.
Word order only: αὐτῶν κοινωνοὶ and κοινωνοὶ αὐτῶν both give 'partakers with them'.

ASV joins the first clause with a colon and no conjunction — 'and scribes: some of them shall ye kill' — while rendering the following καί as 'and some of them shall ye scourge'; the added καί of the RP reading is not represented.
The ASV regularly leaves recitative ὅτι unrendered after 'Verily I say unto you', so the absence of 'that' does not distinguish ἥξει from ὅτι ἥξει.
Word order only: ταῦτα πάντα and πάντα ταῦτα both give 'All these things'.
ἀποκτείνουσα and ἀποκτένουσα are orthographic variants of the same participle; ASV 'that killeth the prophets' renders either.
Word order only: ὄρνις ἐπισυνάγει and ἐπισυνάγει ὄρνις both give 'as a hen gathereth'.
ASV 'under her wings' uses a plain possessive, which renders either αὐτῆς or the reflexive ἑαυτῆς; the ASV does not mark the reflexive here.
ASV text reads 'is left unto you desolate', and its textual_variant note ('Some ancient authorities omit desolate') consigns the omission to the margin; ἔρημος stands in the text.
